description: Set up a habit tracking system with daily check-ins and periodic reviews.

steps.description: Identify habits to build or break and rank them by impact.

outputs.name: habit-list
outputs.desc: Ranked list of habits to build or break

outputs.name: priority-habits
outputs.desc: Top 3 habits to focus on first

process: List all current habits and categorize as build, break, or keep.
Score each by impact on stated goals.
Select the top 3 to focus on first.
Note triggers and barriers for each.

steps.description: Define the tracking method for each habit (streak, frequency, or time-based).

outputs.name: tracking-schema
outputs.desc: Tracking method and metric for each habit

outputs.name: tracking-tools
outputs.desc: Tools or templates to use for tracking

process: Match each habit to a tracking type: streak, frequency count, or duration.
Define the minimum threshold for a successful day.
Select the tracking tool (spreadsheet, app, paper).

steps.description: Design the daily check-in routine for logging habit completion.

outputs.name: checkin-protocol
outputs.desc: Step-by-step daily check-in routine

outputs.name: checkin-template
outputs.desc: Template for the daily log entry

process: Set the check-in time (morning, evening, or both).
Write the check-in steps: open tracker, log each habit, note any blockers.
Design the log entry template with fields for each habit.

steps.description: Design the weekly and monthly review cadence for habit progress.

outputs.name: review-schedule
outputs.desc: Weekly and monthly review dates and agenda

outputs.name: adjustment-criteria
outputs.desc: Rules for when to adjust a habit target

process: Set the weekly review day and questions to answer.
Set the monthly review day for trend analysis.
Define criteria for adjusting targets (e.g., 90% adherence for two weeks means raise the bar).

steps.description: Identify and set up accountability mechanisms.

outputs.name: accountability-plan
outputs.desc: Accountability partners or systems in place

outputs.name: habit-tracking-plan
outputs.desc: Complete habit tracking plan

process: Identify an accountability partner or group.
Set up the reporting mechanism (check-in message, shared tracker).
Define consequences for missed streaks and rewards for milestones.
Compile the full habit tracking plan.

description: Establish a daily journaling practice with prompts, reviews, and action extraction.

steps.description: Select the journaling format that fits your goals and style.

inputs.name: journaling-goals
inputs.desc: What you want from journaling (clarity, gratitude, reflection, creativity)

inputs.name: time-available
inputs.desc: Minutes per day available for journaling

outputs.name: journal-format
outputs.desc: Selected format (freewrite, gratitude, reflection prompts, bullet journal)

outputs.name: format-guidelines
outputs.desc: Rules and structure for the chosen format

process: Match goals to format: clarity maps to freewrite, positivity to gratitude, growth to reflection prompts.
Confirm the format fits the available time.
Write the format guidelines (word count, structure, constraints).

steps.description: Set the daily journaling time, duration, and environment.

outputs.name: journal-schedule
outputs.desc: Daily time, duration, and location for journaling

outputs.name: environment-setup
outputs.desc: Physical or digital setup needed

process: Pick the time of day that aligns with the format (morning for intention setting, evening for reflection).
Set the duration (minimum 5 minutes, maximum matches available time).
Prepare the environment (notebook, app, quiet space).

steps.description: Design a rotating set of journaling prompts.

outputs.name: prompt-library
outputs.desc: Collection of journaling prompts organized by theme

outputs.name: rotation-schedule
outputs.desc: Which prompts to use on which days

process: Write 20-30 prompts organized by theme (gratitude, growth, planning, reflection).
Assign prompts to days of the week or rotate randomly.
Include at least one open-ended freewrite day per week.

steps.description: Review journal entries weekly for themes and action items.

outputs.name: review-protocol
outputs.desc: Weekly review steps for journal entries

outputs.name: action-extraction-method
outputs.desc: How to pull action items from entries

process: Set the weekly review day and time.
Read the week's entries and highlight recurring themes.
Extract any action items or decisions that surfaced.
Note patterns to explore in the next week's prompts.

steps.description: Compile the full journaling framework document.

outputs.name: journaling-framework
outputs.desc: Complete journaling practice document

outputs.name: starter-kit
outputs.desc: First week's prompts and setup checklist

process: Assemble the format, schedule, prompts, and review process into one document.
Write the first week's daily prompts.
Create the setup checklist (materials, environment, calendar blocks).

description: Manage a reading list from collection through notes and application.

steps.description: Collect and organize book and article recommendations.

inputs.name: recommendation-sources
inputs.desc: Where recommendations come from (people, newsletters, lists)

outputs.name: raw-reading-list
outputs.desc: All collected recommendations with source and topic

outputs.name: topic-clusters
outputs.desc: Recommendations grouped by topic

process: Gather all pending recommendations from every source.
Tag each with topic, format (book, article, paper), and source.
Group by topic cluster.

steps.description: Prioritize the reading list by relevance and urgency.

outputs.name: prioritized-list
outputs.desc: Reading list sorted by priority

outputs.name: next-reads
outputs.desc: The next 3-5 items to read

process: Score each item by relevance to current goals (high, medium, low).
Score by time sensitivity (some items lose relevance).
Sort by combined score and select the next 3-5.

steps.description: Schedule dedicated reading blocks in the calendar.

outputs.name: reading-schedule
outputs.desc: Calendar blocks for reading

outputs.name: reading-targets
outputs.desc: Page or article count targets per week

process: Identify available time slots for reading.
Block recurring reading time (daily or weekly).
Set targets: pages per session or articles per week.

steps.description: Take structured notes and highlights while reading.

outputs.name: reading-notes
outputs.desc: Structured notes and highlights per item

outputs.name: key-takeaways
outputs.desc: Top insights from each item

process: Highlight key passages while reading.
Write a one-paragraph summary after each chapter or article.
List the top 3 takeaways per item.

steps.description: Decide what to apply from each reading and plan the application.

outputs.name: application-plan
outputs.desc: Specific actions to take from each reading

outputs.name: reading-list-report
outputs.desc: Complete reading list with notes and status

process: Review the takeaways and select the ones worth acting on.
Write a specific action for each (what, when, how).
Add completed items to the reading log with notes and rating.

description: Declutter your digital life across email, files, photos, and accounts.

steps.description: Audit email subscriptions and unsubscribe from unwanted lists.

inputs.name: declutter-goals
inputs.desc: What a clean inbox looks like to you

outputs.name: subscription-list
outputs.desc: All subscriptions found with keep/unsubscribe decision

outputs.name: unsubscribe-count
outputs.desc: Number of subscriptions removed

process: Scan the inbox for subscription emails over the past 30 days.
Categorize each as keep, unsubscribe, or downgrade frequency.
Unsubscribe from all marked items.
Set a rule to filter remaining subscriptions to a folder.

steps.description: Clean up file storage across desktop, downloads, and cloud drives.

inputs.name: storage-locations
inputs.desc: Folders and drives to clean (desktop, downloads, cloud)

outputs.name: file-inventory
outputs.desc: Organized file structure with deleted and archived counts

outputs.name: folder-structure
outputs.desc: New folder organization system

process: Empty the downloads folder (delete or sort into proper locations).
Clean the desktop to under 10 items.
Organize cloud storage into a consistent folder structure.
Delete duplicates and files older than the retention threshold.

steps.description: Organize photos and media files into a consistent structure.

outputs.name: media-library
outputs.desc: Organized photo and media library

outputs.name: backup-status
outputs.desc: Backup verification for all media

process: Consolidate photos from all devices into one library.
Organize by date and event.
Delete blurry, duplicate, or unwanted photos.
Verify the backup covers all media.

steps.description: Review and close unused online accounts.

inputs.name: email-accounts
inputs.desc: Email accounts to search for sign-up confirmations

outputs.name: account-inventory
outputs.desc: All accounts found with keep/close decision

outputs.name: closed-accounts
outputs.desc: List of accounts closed or deletion requested

process: Search email for account creation confirmations.
Categorize each account as active, dormant, or abandoned.
Close or delete abandoned accounts.
Update passwords on accounts you keep.

steps.description: Set up a recurring maintenance schedule to stay decluttered.

outputs.name: maintenance-schedule
outputs.desc: Recurring tasks to keep digital life clean

outputs.name: declutter-checklist
outputs.desc: Complete declutter checklist with all actions taken

process: Set a monthly email subscription review.
Set a quarterly file storage cleanup.
Set a semi-annual account audit.
Compile the full checklist of everything done and scheduled.

description: Set up a time blocking system based on audited time usage.

steps.description: Audit current time usage by logging activities for one week.

inputs.name: typical-week
inputs.desc: Description of a typical week's activities

outputs.name: time-log
outputs.desc: Detailed log of how time was spent

outputs.name: time-categories
outputs.desc: Activities grouped by type (deep work, meetings, admin, personal)

process: Log every activity in 30-minute blocks for one week.
Categorize each block as deep work, meetings, admin, personal, or transition.
Calculate the percentage of time in each category.
Identify time sinks and unproductive patterns.

steps.description: Design the ideal weekly template based on the time audit.

outputs.name: weekly-template
outputs.desc: Ideal weekly time block template

outputs.name: deep-work-windows
outputs.desc: Protected deep work blocks

process: Allocate time to each category based on priorities, not current habits.
Place deep work in the highest-energy hours.
Group meetings into specific days or time bands.
Leave buffer blocks for overflow and transitions.

steps.description: Block recurring commitments and protect deep work windows.

outputs.name: calendar-blocks
outputs.desc: Recurring calendar events set

outputs.name: protection-rules
outputs.desc: Rules for protecting deep work time

process: Create recurring calendar events for each block type.
Mark deep work blocks as busy and decline conflicting meetings.
Set notification rules (off during deep work, on during admin).

steps.description: Review and adjust the time blocking system weekly.

outputs.name: review-protocol
outputs.desc: Weekly review steps for the time blocking system

outputs.name: time-blocking-template
outputs.desc: Complete time blocking system document

process: Set a weekly review to compare planned vs actual time usage.
Note which blocks held and which were interrupted.
Adjust the template based on what worked.
Compile the full time blocking system document.

description: Set structured goals with milestones, leading indicators, and weekly tracking.

steps.description: Define the life areas to set goals for.

inputs.name: life-areas
inputs.desc: Areas of life to consider (career, health, relationships, finances, learning)

inputs.name: current-situation
inputs.desc: Brief description of where things stand now

outputs.name: focus-areas
outputs.desc: Selected areas to set goals for

outputs.name: area-assessments
outputs.desc: Current state assessment for each area

process: Rate satisfaction in each life area on a 1-10 scale.
Select 2-4 areas with the largest gap between current and desired state.
Write a one-sentence assessment of each selected area.

steps.description: Write goals that are specific and measurable.

outputs.name: goal-statements
outputs.desc: Specific, measurable goal statements

outputs.name: success-criteria
outputs.desc: How to know each goal is achieved

process: Write one goal per focus area with a number and deadline.
Define the success criteria (what does done look like).
Confirm each goal is within your control to achieve.

steps.description: Break each goal into milestones and identify leading indicators.

outputs.name: milestone-map
outputs.desc: Milestones per goal with dates

outputs.name: leading-indicators
outputs.desc: Early signals that progress is on track

process: Break each goal into 3-5 milestones with target dates.
Identify one leading indicator per goal (an early metric that predicts success).
Set the first milestone close enough to build momentum.

steps.description: Set up weekly tracking and the review cadence.

outputs.name: tracking-system
outputs.desc: Weekly tracking method and template

outputs.name: goal-framework
outputs.desc: Complete goal framework document

process: Set a weekly check-in to update leading indicators.
Design the tracking template (goal, milestone, indicator, status).
Set a monthly review to assess milestone progress.
Compile the full goal framework document.

description: Establish a weekly planning ritual from review through time blocking.

steps.description: Review the prior week for wins, misses, and lessons.

inputs.name: week-notes
inputs.desc: Any notes or reflections from the week

outputs.name: week-review
outputs.desc: Summary of wins, misses, and lessons

outputs.name: carryover-items
outputs.desc: Tasks that carry forward to the new week

process: List what was accomplished versus what was planned.
Note the top 3 wins and what made them work.
Note the top 3 misses and what blocked them.
Extract lessons and items to carry forward.

steps.description: Set the top priorities for the upcoming week.

outputs.name: weekly-priorities
outputs.desc: Top 3-5 priorities for the week

outputs.name: task-list
outputs.desc: Full task list for the week

process: Review the calendar for fixed commitments.
Identify the 3-5 most important outcomes for the week.
Break each priority into specific tasks.
Flag any tasks that require preparation or coordination.

steps.description: Time-block the priority tasks into the calendar.

outputs.name: weekly-calendar
outputs.desc: Time-blocked calendar for the week

outputs.name: preparation-list
outputs.desc: Materials and prep needed before the week starts

process: Place priority tasks in the best available time blocks.
Schedule preparation time before tasks that need it.
Leave at least 20% of the week unblocked for reactive work.

steps.description: Set the week's intention and compile the weekly plan.

outputs.name: weekly-intention
outputs.desc: One sentence that captures the week's focus

outputs.name: weekly-plan
outputs.desc: Complete weekly plan document

process: Write one sentence that captures what a successful week looks like.
Compile priorities, calendar, and preparation list into the weekly plan.
Share the plan with anyone who needs to know.

description: Set up an email management system for processing, organizing, and maintaining inbox zero.

steps.description: Define the processing protocol for handling each email.

inputs.name: email-types
inputs.desc: Types of email received (action required, FYI, newsletters, personal)

outputs.name: processing-rules
outputs.desc: Decision tree for handling each email type

outputs.name: processing-windows
outputs.desc: Scheduled times for email processing

process: Define the decision tree: delete, delegate, do (under 2 minutes), defer, or archive.
Set processing windows (e.g., 9am, 1pm, 4pm) instead of continuous checking.
Write the rule for each email type.

steps.description: Set up folders or labels for organized email.

outputs.name: folder-structure
outputs.desc: Folder or label hierarchy

outputs.name: archive-policy
outputs.desc: What gets archived and what gets deleted

process: Create folders aligned with the processing rules (action, waiting, reference, archive).
Keep the folder count under 10 to avoid decision fatigue.
Define the archive vs delete policy.

steps.description: Set up automatic filters and rules for recurring email.

outputs.name: filter-rules
outputs.desc: Automatic filter rules configured

outputs.name: filter-list
outputs.desc: List of all filters with their actions

process: Create filters for newsletters (auto-label, skip inbox).
Create filters for recurring reports (auto-archive or auto-label).
Create filters for high-priority senders (star or flag automatically).

steps.description: Process the inbox to zero and document the system.

outputs.name: inbox-zero-status
outputs.desc: Current inbox count after processing

outputs.name: email-management-plan
outputs.desc: Complete email management system document

process: Process every email in the inbox using the decision tree.
Move each email to the correct folder or archive.
Verify inbox is at zero.
Compile the full email management plan.

description: Design a focused work session protocol for deep work without interruption.

steps.description: Design the focus session format and duration.

inputs.name: work-type
inputs.desc: Type of work to do during focus sessions (writing, coding, analysis)

outputs.name: session-format
outputs.desc: Session structure (pomodoro, 90-minute deep work, custom)

outputs.name: session-rules
outputs.desc: Rules for the session (no phone, no notifications, single task)

process: Select the session format based on work type and attention span.
Set the work and break durations.
Write the session rules (what is allowed and what is not).

steps.description: Identify and eliminate distractions before each session.

outputs.name: distraction-checklist
outputs.desc: Pre-session checklist for eliminating distractions

outputs.name: environment-setup
outputs.desc: Physical and digital environment configuration

process: List the top distractions (phone, email, chat, noise, browser tabs).
Write the elimination step for each (phone in another room, close email, use site blocker).
Set up the physical environment (clean desk, headphones, water).

steps.description: Define the specific goal for each focus session.

outputs.name: goal-template
outputs.desc: Template for setting the session goal

outputs.name: completion-criteria
outputs.desc: How to know the session goal is met

process: Write one sentence stating what will be done by the end of the session.
Define the completion criteria (deliverable, word count, problem solved).
Confirm the goal is achievable in the session length.

steps.description: Log what was accomplished in each session and compile the framework.

outputs.name: session-log-template
outputs.desc: Template for logging session results

outputs.name: focus-session-framework
outputs.desc: Complete focus session protocol document

process: Design the log template: goal, actual outcome, time spent, interruptions, notes.
Set a brief reflection after each session (what worked, what to adjust).
Compile the full focus session framework.

description: Set up a personal knowledge management system for capturing, linking, and reviewing notes.

steps.description: Select the knowledge management tool and method.

inputs.name: note-taking-style
inputs.desc: How you currently take notes (digital, paper, mixed)

inputs.name: knowledge-goals
inputs.desc: What you want the system to do (remember, connect ideas, write from notes)

outputs.name: pkm-method
outputs.desc: Selected method (Zettelkasten, digital garden, wiki, folder system)

outputs.name: pkm-tool
outputs.desc: Selected tool and configuration

process: Match goals to method: connection maps to Zettelkasten, publishing to digital garden, reference to wiki.
Select the tool that supports the method (Obsidian, Notion, LogSeq, plain files).
Configure the tool with the initial folder or tag structure.

steps.description: Define the standard note format and templates.

outputs.name: note-templates
outputs.desc: Templates for each note type (fleeting, literature, permanent)

outputs.name: naming-convention
outputs.desc: File naming and tagging convention

process: Create a template for fleeting notes (quick captures, no structure required).
Create a template for literature notes (source, key points, your reaction).
Create a template for permanent notes (one idea, your own words, linked).
Define the naming and tagging convention.

steps.description: Set up the capture protocol for getting information into the system.

outputs.name: capture-protocol
outputs.desc: Step-by-step process for capturing notes from any source

outputs.name: inbox-setup
outputs.desc: Inbox or capture zone for unprocessed notes

process: Set up a capture inbox (a single place for all unprocessed notes).
Define the capture flow: encounter an idea, open the tool, write a fleeting note.
Set up mobile capture for on-the-go notes.

steps.description: Define the protocol for linking notes by topic and promoting to permanent notes.

outputs.name: linking-rules
outputs.desc: Rules for when and how to link notes

outputs.name: promotion-criteria
outputs.desc: Criteria for promoting a fleeting note to permanent

process: Define linking rules: every permanent note links to at least one other note.
Set promotion criteria: a fleeting note becomes permanent when you can state the idea in your own words.
Schedule a weekly processing session to promote and link notes.

steps.description: Set up the review and pruning schedule and compile the PKM setup plan.

outputs.name: review-schedule
outputs.desc: Schedule for reviewing and pruning the knowledge base

outputs.name: pkm-setup-plan
outputs.desc: Complete PKM setup document

process: Set a weekly review to process the inbox and link new notes.
Set a monthly review to prune outdated or low-value notes.
Compile the full PKM setup plan with method, tool, templates, protocols, and schedule.
